question: Which of the following values is subtracted from the numerical value of temperature expressed in Kelvin to obtain the temperature in degrees Celsius ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**273**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To convert a temperature from Kelvin to degrees Celsius, you subtract **273** from the Kelvin value.
 
• The Kelvin scale is an absolute temperature scale starting from absolute zero, which is 0 K.
 
• The Celsius scale is a relative temperature scale where 0 degrees Celsius is the freezing point of water.
 
• The formula for conversion is: Temperature in °C=Temperature in K−273" id="MathJax-Element-2-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Temperature in °C=Temperature in K−273Temperature in °C=Temperature in K−273" id="MathJax-Element-3-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Temperature in °C=Temperature in K−273Temperature in °C=Temperature in K−273
 Temperature in °C=Temperature in K−273
 \text{Temperature in °C} = \text{Temperature in K} - 273 .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Kelvin scale is named after the physicist William Thomson, 1st Baron Kelvin.
 
• Absolute zero (0 K) is the lowest temperature possible, where all molecular motion ceases.
 
• The Celsius scale is named after the Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius.
 
• Both Kelvin and Celsius scales are used in scientific contexts, but Kelvin is preferred for thermodynamic temperature measurements.
